potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract A method for skeletal editing of C–C σ-bonds in strained alicycles via single-carbon insertion is reported. This skeletal editing method for cyclobutanols differs from well-established semipinacol rearrangement pathways, offering an efficient route to cyclopentanols by direct scaffold hopping of cyclobutanols. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions in good yields, expanding the toolkit for single-atom insertion into C–C σ-bonds.

potentialGaps.title: Planar Bis(1,3,4-Oxadiazole) Bridging toward High-Energy and Low-Sensitivity Tetracyclic Compounds
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract A planar bis(1,3,4-oxadiazole) bridging strategy was developed to access rigid, extended-conjugated tetracyclic energetic compounds. Incorporation of this bridge into two distinct energetic scaffolds afforded 4 and 7. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction revealed a nearly planar bis(1,3,4-oxadiazole) bridge in both compounds, accompanied by extended π-electron delocalization across the molecular frameworks. Compound 4 showed enhanced thermal and mechanical stability, while 7 combined improved energetic performance with increased stability.

potentialGaps.title: Scaffold Hopping of Pyrimidines into 2-Acylpyrroles
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract A practical skeletal-editing strategy was developed for the conversion of 4-substituted pyrimidines into 2-acyl-5-arylpyrroles. The transformation directly converts a six-membered, electron-deficient pyrimidine into a five-membered azole while simultaneously installing an acyl group. The reaction sequence involves pyrimidine activation, ring-opening, fragmentation, and ring reconstruction. Central to this strategy is the controlled generation of pyrimidine-derived vinamidinium salts as open-chain A4 synthons, which are then intercepted by α-bromoketones as functionalized annulation reagents. The developed scaffold-hopping method can be applied for late-stage modification of pyrimidine-containing bioactive or pharmaceutical molecules.

potentialGaps.title: Solid-Phase Synthesis of Enteropeptin A Analogues
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Enteropeptin A is a sactipeptide natural product featuring a unique six-membered thiomorpholine core. Herein, we describe a solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS)-compatible approach to enteropeptin A analogues featuring a simplified sactionine motif. The strategy employs a readily accessible building block and efficient on-resin assembly. A “N to C” variant, differing in the directionality of the sactionine linkage was also readily accessible. Collectively, this work accelerates access to analogues of this important class of natural products.

potentialGaps.title: Stereoselective Synthesis of Linustedastat Via Deoxy-Aromatization Strategy
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract An efficient and stereoselective synthesis of Linustedastat (1) is reported, commencing from inexpensive and commercially available sitolactone. The route features a highly chemoselective Grignard addition, followed by sequential double aldol condensations to construct the core steroidal framework. A key step involves a novel deoxy-aromatization of a fluorinated steroid intermediate, setting the stage for a stereoselective hydrogenation and a 1,4-conjugate addition to further elaborate the molecule. This strategically designed sequence delivers the complex and electron-deficient fluorinated steroidal architecture in 16 steps with an 11.0% overall yield.

potentialGaps.title: Synthesis of α-Cyano-β-naphthylamines via Tandem Selective Hydrocyanation of Unactivated Alkynes and Thorpe Reaction
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract An unprecedented nickel-catalyzed tandem reaction involving alkyne hydrocyanation and sequential Thorpe reaction has been developed. By employing readily available and less toxic Zn(CN)2 as the cyanide source, both selective alkyne hydrocyanation and tandem cyclization are achieved in a substrate-controlled manner. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations confirm that the alkenyl nitrile serves as a key intermediate, and hydrogen transfer is identified as the rate-determining step in the Thorpe reaction. This work offers a novel strategy for the construction of α-cyano-β-naphthylamine via a cascade reaction mode.

potentialGaps.title: Divergent Kinetics and Rate-Determining Steps for 1-Butene and 2-Butene Hydroformylation with a Bidentate Phosphoramidite Ligand: A Combined Experimental and Density Functional Theory Study
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The hydroformylation of mixed butenes (1-butene and 2-butene) to n-valeraldehyde is an important industrial process, yet the distinct kinetic behaviors of the two isomers under identical catalytic conditions remain insufficiently understood. Herein, a comprehensive kinetic and mechanistic investigation of 1-butene and 2-butene was conducted using a robust, water- and air-stable, highly regioselective bidentate phosphoramidite ligand-modified rhodium catalyst in a homogeneous system. Systematic kinetic experiments revealed that the hydroformylation of 2-butene exhibits a strong positive dependence on H2 pressure and obvious substrate inhibition at high concentrations, whereas 1-butene shows little H2 dependence and no substrate inhibition. Using a semi-empirical hyperbolic kinetic modeling, the rate equations capture these distinct behaviors with high accuracy (R2 = 0.9746 for 2-butene, 0.9642 for 1-butene). Kinetic studies revealed distinct rate behaviors for 1-butene and 2-butene hydroformylation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations on the n-valeraldehyde pathway further showed that hydride insertion to the internal C═C double bond has the highest barrier for 2-butene, while CO insertion to the linear rhodium n-butyl intermediate has the highest barrier for 1-butene, providing the mechanistic origin for the observed kinetic differences. The iso-valeraldehyde pathway is additionally disfavored by a 2.7 kcal·mol–1 higher RDS barrier, consistent with the good n-selectivity. In situ high-pressure FTIR spectroscopy further confirmed the five-coordinate hydride HRh(CO)2(P)2 as the catalyst resting state. These findings offer quantitative guidance for optimizing industrial hydroformylation processes using mixed butene feedstocks.

potentialGaps.title: Architecting 3D Space‐Charge Heterointerfacial Networks for Electrode‐Scale Ion Transport
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing space‐charge effects to govern carrier dynamics is central to nanoionics, yet translating localized nanoscale transport into continuous electrode‐wide percolation remains challenging. Here, we report an architectural strategy that uses Na 2 O/Na 2 CO 3 heterointerfaces as local nanoionic transport units and organizes them into a bulk‐distributed, three‐dimensional network throughout a preformed electrode. This architecture is realized by coupling ultralow‐flux Na‐vapor metallization with mesopore‐regulated gas‐solid conversion in a preformed metal‐organic framework (MOF) host. The synergy of space‐charge carrier enrichment and MOF‐mediated lattice distortion simultaneously boosts carrier density and lowers migration barriers, yielding an estimated local interfacial conductivity on the order of 10 −7 S cm −1 at 25°C, from intrinsically insulating Na 2 O (10 −12 S cm −1 ) and Na 2 CO 3 (10 −23 S cm −1 ). Integrated with conducting carbon, this functionally percolating network enables stable solid‐state presodiation and ultrahigh‐rate sodium‐ion full cells. This work bridges the gap between nanoscopic interface physics and macroscopic device functionality, identifying the spatial connectivity of phase boundaries, rather than the localized space‐charge effect alone, as a programmable design variable for next‐generation solid‐state ionics.

potentialGaps.title: Generation and Stabilization of Soliton‐Type Radicals in Amidine‐Linked Porous Oligoacetylene Polymers by Topological Confinement Strategy for Photothermal Catalysis
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Porous polymers incorporating stable organic radicals are typically limited to a handful of known radical types. Here, we introduce a topological confinement strategy that generates a previously inaccessible class of open‑shell species: neutral soliton‑type radicals, within amidine‑linked oligoacetylene networks. In chemical terms, these species are characterized by a delocalized spin density over the conjugated backbone, distinguishing them from conventional localized radicals. These materials exhibit a distinct axial g ‑tensor, Curie behavior, and broad near‑infrared absorption extending to 1000 nm. Unlike conventional photothermal systems, where heat originates from exciton transfer energy to the lattice via nonradiative processes, our system stores light energy in long‐lived soliton states that dissipate via lattice vibrations, producing no ground‑state bleach yet enabling efficient heat generation. Using this mechanism, the materials drive aldehyde‑indole coupling under mild light irradiation through a photothermal catalytic pathway. More broadly, this work translates soliton physics into a synthetic materials platform for spin‑functional materials.

potentialGaps.title: Hierarchically Molecular Programming of Antiparallel H‑Aggregates for NIR Type I Photochemistry
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing near‐infrared (NIR) photosensitizers with effective type I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation remains challenging. H‑aggregates promote triplet formation and charge transfer, but often suffer from substantial absorption blueshifts and excessive thermal deactivation that compromise photosensitization efficacy. Herein, a hierarchically molecular programming strategy is proposed to construct minimal‐blueshift H‐aggregates as robust NIR type I photosensitizers. Primary engineering via π‐bridge extension and acceptor strengthening within a twisted–planar donor–π–acceptor scaffold endows the antiparallel H‐packed TNCF3‐C6‐C2 aggregates with strong NIR absorption (749 nm) and predominant type I ROS generation. Secondary side‐chain programming further regulates the H‐packing and intermolecular electronic interactions to enhance type I ROS generation. Structural, photochemical and theoretical investigations revealed that the branched side chains promote molecular planarization and robust H‑packing, thereby enhancing intersystem crossing and intermolecular charge transfer. The optimized TNCF3‐2C6 with symmetric branched side chain exhibited minimal absorption blueshift (20 nm) upon H‐aggregation, enhanced NIR harvesting ability and a further ∼2‐fold enhancement in ROS generation over the initial TNCF3‐C6‐C2 H‐aggregates, thereby delivering potent tumor inhibition both in vitro and in vivo. Built upon the hierarchical programming of H‐aggregates, this work establishes a supramolecular design paradigm toward modulating excitonic coupling and excited‐state dynamics for high‐performance photo‐functional materials.

Synthesis of Pyrido[2,3- d ]pyrimidin-4(3 H )-ones via SNAr/Tandem Cyclization
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract A new method has been developed for constructing the pyrido[2,3-d]pyrimidin-4(3H)-one scaffold under metal- and ligand-free conditions. In this strategy, 2-bromo-N-phenylnicotinamide is activated by the synergistic electron-withdrawing effects of the pyridine ring and the amide group, enabling tandem nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr)/cyclization with cyanamide or formamide under simple conditions. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support an SNAr/cyclization mechanism. Preliminary photophysical studies show that the products exhibit blue emission, suggesting potential applications in materials science. Additionally, molecular docking studies indicate that the synthesized scaffold may have relevance to medicinal chemistry, providing a foundation for future biological evaluations.

Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets
potentialGaps.abstract: Single-cell genomics enables cell-resolved insights into in-situ microbial communities, yet single amplified genomes (SAGs) are often fragmented, taxonomically ambiguous, and prone to contamination, limiting their biological interpretation. Here, we present Scellmate, a scalable, semi-supervised framework that integrates whole-SAG curation, species-level taxonomic anchoring and SAG–mobilome linkage analysis for large-scale SAG datasets. Following benchmarking of its SAG curation and SAG–eMGE linkage modules using in silico and four-strain mock SAG datasets, respectively, Scellmate was applied to 11,976 sewage-derived SAGs. This approach yielded 4,198 SAGs passing Scellmate’s whole-SAG curation, which captured pronounced heterogeneity masked by bulk methods. At the species level, we resolved extensive hidden diversity within abundant taxa such as Aliarcobacter that was unresolved by matched metagenome-assembled genomes; at the strain level, we pinpointed a distinct Agathobacter rectalis cluster carrying specialized carbon-utilization pathways, suggesting niche differentiation. Leveraging these curated SAGs, we identified 6,474 host–mobilome linkages across 2,378 SAGs; these linkages not only showed high concordance with host-association data within the Integrated Microbial Genomes (IMG) system but also significantly expanded species-level host assignments. Furthermore, we detected frequent inter-species sharing patterns of diverse cryptic plasmids within the order Bacteroidales. Together, this work demonstrates that high-throughput single-cell genomics, empowered by the robust framework, resolves fine-scale heterogeneity and host–mobilome dynamics, advancing culture-independent microbiome research. potentialGaps.title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
potentialGaps.abstract: Despite the growing global demand for end-of-life care resulting from rapid social transformations, significant gaps exist in cross-national research examining unmet end-of-life care needs. Using harmonized end-of-life survey data (2010-2021) from the United States, 28 European countries, South Korea, China, and Mexico, here we show that the United States, Europe, and South Korea exhibit higher overall unmet end-of-life care needs than China and Mexico, where limited formal care provision is compensated with high levels of informal care. Death at institutions is associated with lower overall unmet end-of-life care needs in the United States and South Korea, with Mexico presenting an exception. Similarly, urban areas in Europe and South Korea exhibit lower unmet formal end-of-life care needs compared to rural areas. Among married individuals, only Mexico exhibits significantly lower unmet overall end-of-life care needs compared to unmarried individuals. Having children is consistently linked to lower unmet informal end-of-life care needs across the United States, Europe, and South Korea. Our findings highlight the complex interplay between care systems and family demographic structures in shaping end-of-life care access, and underscore the need for tailored policy approaches that strengthen both formal and informal care systems while addressing sociodemographic disparities in care access. Formal end-of-life care expansion in the US, Europe, and South Korea has not fully compensated for declining informal care, resulting in care gaps. Demographic transitions interact with development contexts to create distinct care landscapes.
topics: Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health

potentialGaps.title: Umpolung Strain-Release Ring Opening of Carbonyl Bicyclo[1.1.0]butane Aldehydes Enabled by N -Heterocyclic Carbene Catalyzed Redox Esterification
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract A new type of carbonyl BCB aldehydes was synthesized through oxidation of vinyl-carbonyl BCBs. Under the catalysis of 10 mol % N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC), these BCB aldehydes underwent redox esterification with various primary, secondary alcohols and phenols to afford 1,3-dicarbonyl substituted cyclobutanes in 61%–99% yields. Mechanism study indicates the carbonyl group can activate BCB aldehyde and assist to stabilize the enolate intermediate, which is critical for the success of this reaction.
